old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a sparkler against a pitch-black background. The sparkler is positioned centrally, emitting a bright, intense light at its core. From this central point, numerous thin, elongated sparks radiate outward in all directions, creating a dynamic and mesmerizing display. These sparks vary in brightness and intensity, with some appearing as bright white points while others are slightly dimmer, adding depth to the visual effect. The sparks move continuously, giving the impression of a lively and ever-changing pattern. The overall scene is one of vibrant energy and excitement, typical of a festive or celebratory moment. There are no other objects or characters present in the video, focusing solely on the sparkler's brilliant display. The camera remains stationary throughout, ensuring that the viewer's attention is entirely on the sparkler's captivating performance.

caption: The video captures a close-up view of a burning sparkler set against a uniformly dark background. A bright yellow-white combustion point occupies the center of the frame, with a short orange-red stick visible just below it. From this tip, numerous thin golden spark trails radiate outward in a starburst pattern, several ending in small star-like flares. The sparkler is already burning at the first frame and continues burning steadily through the last frame, the bright central tip and the orange-red stick persisting without extinguishing. The configuration of radiating spark trails changes from frame to frame. Thin streaks continuously shoot outward, extend, and fade, so the overall starburst flickers and reshapes while remaining centered on the tip. A few isolated sparks appear detached from the main burst near the frame edges, positioned farther from the tip than the dense inner spray. The bright tip and stick drift only slightly within the frame, staying approximately centered the whole time.

on the first frame and still be happening after the last. Do not force the endpoints to match,
infer a physical error from their mismatch, or manufacture continuity across a visible edit.
Use the chronological video as primary evidence. The independent visual notes are fallible aids,
not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.
Retain its English narrative voice, viewpoint, paragraph structure and level of visual detail.
Aim for 85-115% of the original WISA word count,
and retain supported scene details while clearly describing the main visible process. Do not
replace it with a short keyword prompt, physics explanation, checklist or a generic summary.
Correct wrong subjects, actions, directions, contacts, temporal ordering and completion claims.
Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
Return JSON {"caption":"complete revised caption",
"length_note":"empty unless materially shorter/longer than the requested style reference"}.
